turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't want to be a bother, but he didn't think it was a good time for games, considering Miss Havisham was not feeling well.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, he wastes his time with excuses, no doubt. He is to call Estella at once, and bring her to Miss Havisham, that they may resume their interrupted play.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He felt a bit more bold, but still a trifle anxious, and said to Miss Havisham that he was afraid it wouldn't be a good time for games, considering she wasn't feeling quite herself.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, he dare not address Miss Havisham with such impertinence, Miss Havisham wonders if he has any notion of propriety at all.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He wondered if it would be right to go and fetch Estella, when Miss Havisham didn't seem quite well, but he also didn't want to be disobedient.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, he thinks to coddle Miss Havisham, but she knows her own mind, and she will not be swayed by his feeble excuses.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't know as it was right to fetch Estella, not when Miss Havisham didn't seem quite herself, but he didn't want to displease her neither.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, he thinks to stand on ceremony with her, but she will not be swayed by such petty considerations. She commands him to fetch Estella at once, and to bring the child to her with all due haste.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't know if it was right to fetch Estella, not being sure if Miss Havisham was truly unwell, and he didn't want to get into trouble either.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, still hesitating and making excuses, does he not know that Miss Havisham's patience is wearing thin?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't mean to be disobedient, Miss Havisham, only he didn't know if it was proper to fetch Estella when she might be busy or not feeling well.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, still dawdling and making excuses, does he not know that Miss Havisham's time is being wasted by his indecision?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't know if fetching Estella was such a good idea, Miss Havisham, not being sure if it would be proper for him to fetch her when she might be... um... occupied

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, he will not be silenced, Miss Havisham will not be trifled with, and he will fetch Estella at once.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: he didn't know if Miss Havisham would be pleased for him to play games with Estella, not being used to such company

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, if he wishes to continue in Miss Havisham's service, he must learn to address her with the respect due to her station, and not dawdle with petty excuses.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: he didn't want to trouble Miss Havisham with his humble games, not being worthy of such attention

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, he thinks to decline Miss Havisham's invitation to play with Estella? Never! It is his duty to amuse her, and he will do it, or suffer the consequences.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: he didn't want to disobey Miss Havisham, but he had to think of his sister, Magwitch, and her troubles, and the family's poverty, and how it might be better for him to stay with them

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, he thinks his family's poverty is a concern of Miss Havisham's? It is not her duty to feed or clothe them, it is his own duty to provide for them, and for that he must be away from them, to learn the ways of the world.

opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy and had come to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer and let her look at him.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not afraid.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched when she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he knew it was her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that her heart was broken.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired and wanted diversion.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies and had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham repeatedly told Pip to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not sullen and obstinate, but was very sorry for Miss Havisham and could not play just now.
